content: Finance wants a fix out before the holidays. Can I cut a release on December 22nd?

Not by default. December 22nd falls inside the year-end code freeze (Dec 15 to Jan 5), while Finance runs the annual close. No production release may go out in that window, hotfixes included, unless a lead in #fin-eng signs off in the channel first.

Your options:

- **Release before the freeze.** Tag by Dec 14. That means finishing the release checklist in the PR template and getting a billing-team member to approve the production promotion in the CI UI. Staging promotes automatically.
- **Ask for a freeze exception.** If the fix can't make it before Dec 15, post in #fin-eng and get a lead's sign-off before tagging. Since the fix is for Finance, the exception may be easy to get, but the sign-off has to come first.

If you get the sign-off, Dec 22 is a Tuesday, so the Friday-after-14:00-UTC rule doesn't apply. You'd tag `v2026.12.N` from main and let CI publish. Any database migrations the fix needs must ship in the same release.

I took this from the project's recorded release process. I haven't checked it against the CI config or any other calendar, so confirm the dates with the team if the freeze window might have changed.
